title: Adoption mode: a new osf.toml key and its gate
summary: Adds a top-level `adoption_mode` key to a repository's own `osf.toml`, read by a new `config::adoption_mode` and enforced by `config::require_adoption_mode`, which refuses to run a command unless the configured mode is one the command declares it supports. Only one mode exists so far, `private-factory-repo`; no command depends on it yet. The layered config loader is taught to drop the key so it never trips `deny_unknown_fields`, and the development docs describe the key and its values.

nodes.label: Layered config files
nodes.subtitle: user / project / file layers
nodes.summary: The config files merged by `load`. They are parsed into a struct with `deny_unknown_fields`, so any key the struct does not know must be stripped before the merge.

nodes.label: adoption_mode()
nodes.subtitle: fn adoption_mode(root: &Path) -> Result<Option<AdoptionMode>, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: Reads `<root>/osf.toml`, returns `None` when the file or the key is absent, parses the string against `AdoptionMode::ALL`, and errors naming the key and the supported values when the value is unknown or the file is not valid TOML.

nodes.label: require_adoption_mode()
nodes.subtitle: fn require_adoption_mode(root, command, supported) -> Result<AdoptionMode, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The gate a command calls: reads the key and checks the mode against the list the command supports. An unset key is refused as well, so a command never runs on a guessed mode.

nodes.label: AdoptionMode
nodes.subtitle: enum AdoptionMode { PrivateFactoryRepo }
nodes.summary: The mode vocabulary: `KEY` names the config key, `ALL` lists every supported mode, `name()` gives the value written in osf.toml, and `parse()` maps a raw string back to a variant. A later mode adds a variant and a name in `ALL`.

nodes.label: load()
nodes.subtitle: fn load(...) -> Result<Config, ConfigError>
nodes.summary: The layered loader. It now removes `adoption_mode` from each file's table before merging, exactly as it already removes `review` and `agents`, so the key never trips the struct's `deny_unknown_fields`.

nodes.label: review_config()
nodes.subtitle: [review] section reader
nodes.summary: The existing sibling reader for the `[review]` table of the same file. It establishes the pattern the new adoption-mode reader follows: read the file, pull one entry, error with the path and the offending value.

nodes.label: agents_config()
nodes.subtitle: [agents] section reader
nodes.summary: The existing sibling reader for the `[agents]` table, and the function the new code is inserted directly after.

nodes.label: config tests
nodes.subtitle: mod tests
nodes.summary: Five new tests: the key is unset when the file or key is absent, the one supported value parses, an unsupported value is refused naming the key and the values, `require_adoption_mode` refuses a command whose supported list excludes the configured mode and refuses an unset key, and the layered load ignores the key.
